title: The Part Apollo 13 Couldn’t Be Sent
narration: NASA needed a part it couldn't send. The Apollo 13 crew had square carbon dioxide filters, but their lifeboat needed a different connection. Engineers on Earth designed an adapter using materials already aboard. The astronauts built it. The carbon dioxide level fell, and those extra filters could finally do their job.

fact_sources.supports: Command-module square lithium-hydroxide canisters did not fit the lunar-module system; ground team adapted them using onboard materials.
Engineering team tested an adapter with replicas of onboard supplies, the crew assembled it, and CO2 levels dropped after installation.
Primary historical account of ground/crew cooperation and limited onboard materials.
